Rashi on Shabbat 12a:10:2.hebrew: מתירין - כדמפרש טעמא בפרק שמונה שרצים (לקמן שבת דף קז:), מאילים מאדמים דמשכן: מה אילים פרים ורבים, אף כל שפרה ורבה; וכינה אינה פרה ורבה, אלא מבשר אדם היא שורצת:
Rashi on Shabbat 12a:10:2.english: [Beit Hillel] permit - As the reason is explained in chapter Shemonah Sheratzim (below, Shabbat 107b), [derived] from the red-dyed rams of the Tabernacle: Just as rams procreate, so too anything that procreates; and a louse does not procreate, but rather it swarms from human flesh.

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:11:1.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar would also say - That in these [matters] as well, Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel disagree.

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:11:2.english: One may not make matches - [This applies] on Shabbat, because of [the verse], "from pursuing your affairs."

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:11:3.english: And Beit Hillel permit - For they hold: "Your affairs" [are forbidden], but not the affairs of Heaven.

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:11:4.english: And one may not comfort [mourners] - Because he is distressed along with those who are in distress.

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:12:1.english: It is Shabbat, [which precludes one] from crying out - One must put their minds at ease with words of consolation, so that they will not be distressed.

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:12:2.english: It is capable of having mercy - If you honor it [by refraining] from being distressed on it.

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:1:1.hebrew: שלא ילקה כו' - דהיינו אצולי טינוף, לא חשיב ליה הך כפיי':
Rashi on Shabbat 12a:1:1.english: That [the wall] will not be damaged, etc. - That is, preventing soiling — [the Tanna] does not consider this overturning [to be significant].

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:1:2.hebrew: מי דמי - הא לא ניחא ליה בהנך משקין כלל, וברצונו לא ירדו. ונהי נמי דכפיית קערה חשיבא ליה — אנן חשיבותא דמשקין בעינן, וכפייה זו אינה אלא לגלות עליהן שאינו חפץ בהן. אבל הכא, לענין שבת, אחשיבותא דהוצאה קפדינן, והך הוצאה דכיס חשיבא, דקא מיבעי ליה להציל על בגדיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 12a:1:2.english: Are [these cases] comparable? - Behold, he is not pleased with those liquids at all, and they did not fall with his consent. And even granted that the overturning of the bowl is significant to him, we require the significance of the liquids, and this overturning only serves to reveal about them that he does not desire them. However, here, with regard to Shabbat, we are particular about the significance of the carrying out; and this carrying out of the pouch is significant, as he needs it to protect his garments.

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:2:1.hebrew: הא לא דמיא - ע"כ, אם להכשר זרעים באת לדמויה, לא תדמיה אלא להך:
Rashi on Shabbat 12a:2:1.english: This is not comparable - Perforce, if you have come to compare it to [the laws of] rendering seeds susceptible [to ritual impurity], do not compare it except to this [case].

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:2:2.hebrew: שירד דלף לתוכה כו' - משנה היא במסכת מכשירין (פ"ד משנה ה), השנויה אחר הסיפא דהכופה את הקערה. והכי תנן: עריבה שירד הדלף לתוכה כו', הניחה שירד הדלף לתוכה — מים הניתזין והצפים: ב"ש אומרים, בכי יותן; וב"ה אומרים, אינם בכי יותן. נטלה לשופכה — אלו ואלו מודים שהן בכי יותן. ומ"מ יש לשמוע מהך סיפא, כדגרסינן בספרים (וכב"ה): נתנה לעריבה זו שירד הדלף לתוכה — אע"ג דאצולי טינוף הוא, אפילו הכי, מדלא כפאה, גלי דעתי' דאחשבינהו לקבלן, והוו חשובים אותן שבתוכה. והך הוצאה נמי, אחשבה לקבולי בהאי כיס האי זיבה; אע"ג דבזיבה לא ניחא ליה, אנן לחיובי אהוצאת זיבה לא מהדרינן, אלא אהוצאת כיס:
Rashi on Shabbat 12a:2:2.english: That a roof-drip fell into it, etc. - This is a mishna in Tractate Makhshirin (chapter 4, mishna 5), taught after the latter clause of [the mishna regarding] one who overturns a bowl. And this is what we learned [there]: “A trough into which the roof-drip fell, etc. [If] he placed it so that the roof-drip would fall into it — [as for] water that splashes out and that overflows: Beit Shammai say: [It is] subject to 'if [water] be put'; and Beit Hillel say: [It is] not subject to 'if [water] be put'. [If] he took it to pour it out — both agree that they are subject to 'if [water] be put'.” And nevertheless, one can deduce from this latter clause [what] we read in our books (and according to Beit Hillel): [Where] he placed this trough so that the roof-drip would fall into it — even though it is [only] to prevent soiling, even so, since he did not overturn it, he revealed his intention that he considered them important to collect them, and those [waters] that are inside it become significant. And [regarding] this carrying out as well, he considered it significant [in order] to receive this emission in this pouch; even though he is not pleased with the emission, we do not seek to hold [him] liable for carrying out the emission, but rather for carrying out the pouch.

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:2:4.english: And that which overflows - From the top when [the bowl] is full.

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:2:5.english: Are not [subject to the law of] “if [water] be put” - For he is not pleased with them.

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:3:1.hebrew: הא רבי יהודה - דאמר: מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה — שברצונו לא תעשה, ואינו צריך לעיקר (תחלתה) [תכליתה], כי הכא, שאינו צריך לזיבה זו שעל ידה בא הכיס הזה — ואעפ"כ חייב עליה. ופלוגתייהו בהמצניע (לקמן שבת דף צג:), גבי מוציא המת במטה חייב, ואע"ג דהוצאת המת לא ניחא ליה ביה; ור"ש פוטר:
Rashi on Shabbat 12a:3:1.english: This is [according to] Rabbi Yehuda - For he said [that with regard to] a labor not needed for its own sake — which would not be done of his own will, and he does not need the essence of (its beginning) [its ultimate purpose], as [is the case] here, where he does not need this discharge on account of which this pouch came [about] — nevertheless, he is liable for it. And their dispute is in [the chapter] HaMatznia (below, Shabbat 93b), regarding [the ruling that] one who carries out a corpse in a bed is liable, even though the carrying out of the corpse is not pleasing to him; and Rabbi Shimon exempts [him].

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:4:1.english: At nightfall - And we are not concerned that perhaps he will go out with them once it gets dark.

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:4:2.hebrew: והיה על מצחו תמיד - קרא יתירא הוא להך דרשה, דהא כבר קבע ליה מקום: "והיה על מצח אהרן":
Rashi on Shabbat 12a:4:2.english: And it shall be always upon his forehead - It is a superfluous verse for this exposition, for it already established its place: "And it shall be upon Aaron's forehead."

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:4:3.hebrew: למשמש בבגדו - שלא יהא כרוך בשום דבר, פן יוציאנו:
Rashi on Shabbat 12a:4:3.english: To feel his garment - So that it not be wrapped around anything, lest he carry it out.

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:4:4.english: A great halakha - There is a great matter here, to keep him away from a prohibition of Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:5:1.hebrew: שמא יהרוג - וביום נמי עסקינן, ולאור הנר דמתני' אלא יקרא קאי:
Rashi on Shabbat 12a:5:1.english: Lest he kill - And we are dealing even during the day, and "by the light of the lamp" in the mishna applies only to "he may not read".

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:5:2.english: Like one who kills a camel - That is to say, [an animal] that is very large.

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:5:3.hebrew: או דילמא - לאור הנר דקתני — אתרוייהו קאי, ותרוייהו — שמא יטה, אבל ביום שפיר דמי:
Rashi on Shabbat 12a:5:3.english: Or perhaps - [The phrase] "by the light of the lamp" that is taught applies to both of them, and both of them [are forbidden] lest he tilt [the lamp], but during the day it is permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:6:1.hebrew: מי אלימא ממתניתין - דקתני לאור הנר בסוף, ואפ"ה מספקא לן, דאיכא לפלוגי בהו ולמימר דלאור הנר אלא יקרא קאי. הכא נמי איכא למימר דאין פולין אפילו ביום, ולאור הנר אאין קורין קאי:
Rashi on Shabbat 12a:6:1.english: Is it stronger than our Mishnah? - For [the Mishnah] taught “by candlelight” at the end, and even so we were uncertain, since one can differentiate between them and say that “by candlelight” refers [only] to “he may not read.” Here too, one can say that “one may not delouse” [applies] even by day, and “by candlelight” refers [only] to “one may not read.”

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:7:1.english: Come and hear - For it teaches "by the light of the lamp" regarding both of them.

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:8:1.hebrew: בני מחוזא - מפנקי, ולא עבדי מלאכה, ובגדיהם רחבים כשל אשה, וצריכים עיון:
Rashi on Shabbat 12a:8:1.english: The people of Meḥoza - They are pampered and do not perform labor, and their garments are wide like those of a woman and require scrutiny.

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:8:2.hebrew: מידע ידעי - שבגדי האנשים קצרין, שעוסקין בשדות במלאכה, ושל נשים — רחבים בתי יד שלהן:
Rashi on Shabbat 12a:8:2.english: They know - For men's garments are short, as they engage in labor in the fields, and women's [garments] have wide sleeves.

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:8:3.hebrew: דזקנות - קצרים במקצת, ושל אנשים מעונגין רחבים, ודומין זה לזה, וגזרינן שמא יטה:
Rashi on Shabbat 12a:8:3.english: [Those] of elderly women - [Their garments] are somewhat short, and those of pampered men are wide, and they resemble one another; and we decree [a prohibition] lest he tilt [the lamp].

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:8:4.hebrew: אבל דילדות - רחבים הרבה, ואין של אנשים דומין להם:
Rashi on Shabbat 12a:8:4.english: But [those] of young women - [They are] very wide, and those of men do not resemble them.

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:9:1.english: In the public domain - [This applies] on a weekday.

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:9:2.hebrew: מפני הכבוד - של עוברין, שלא ימאסו:
Rashi on Shabbat 12a:9:2.english: In deference to dignity - [The dignity] of passersby, so that they will not be disgusted.

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:9:3.english: Appiktoizin - Vomiting — gomite in Old French. So I found [written].

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:9:4.hebrew: מולל וזורק - בשבת, מולל להתיש כחן שלא יחזרו אליו, ובלבד שלא ימלול בדוחק ויהרוג, דסבירא ליה הריגת כינה שבות. ואבא שאול כר"א ומחייב חטאת. הלכך, גזרינן מלילה שלא יהרוג:
Rashi on Shabbat 12a:9:4.english: Rolls and throws - On Shabbat, he rolls [them] to weaken their strength so that they do not return to him, provided that he does not roll [them] forcefully and kill [them], for he holds that killing a louse is [only] a rabbinic prohibition (shevut). And Abba Shaul holds in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer and deems [one] liable to a sin-offering; therefore, we decree against rolling, lest he kill [them].

Rashi on Shabbat 12a:9:5.english: Would sever them - He would kill them, and [he did so] on Shabbat.

Tosafot on Shabbat 12a:2:1.hebrew: ושבתוכה הרי זה בכי יותן - אין זה במשנה, אלא שהש"ס מדקדק: מדנקט "הניתזין והניצפין אינן בכי יותן", משמע: הא שבתוכה — הרי הן בכי יותן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 12a:2:1.english: "And that which is inside it is under 'if [water] be placed'" - This is not in the Mishnah; rather, the Gemara deduces [it]: From [the fact] that it stated, "The [water that] splashes and overflows is not under 'if [water] be placed,'" it implies that that which is inside it is under 'if [water] be placed'.

Tosafot on Shabbat 12a:5:1.hebrew: שמא יהרוג - פירש הרב יוסף מאורליינ"ש, דכינה היינו שחורה הקופצת, דכתיב: "והך את עפר הארץ והיה לכנים" (שמות ח׳:י״ב), ודרך שחורה הקופצת לצאת מן הארץ, ובזאת נחלקו עליו רבנן. אבל פרעוש היא הכינה הרוחשת, וחייב עליה אפילו לרבנן, כדאמרי' בפ' שמונה שרצים (לקמן ' ף קז: ושם). ואין נראה לר"ת, דאמרינן במדרש: "אף כי אנוש רמה" — אלו כנים שבראש. ובנדה פ"ב (דף כ:): "שלח לה מסריקותא מקטל קלמי", ופי' בקונטרס: מסרק להרוג כנים; ואין דרך שחורה הקופצת להיות בראש. ועוד, בברכות (פ"ז דף נא:) אמרינן: "ממהדורי מילי ומסמרטוטי קלמי", ודרך כנים לבנות הרוחשות להיות בסמרטוטי מבגדים ישנים. ועוד, דפרעוש אמר לקמן בפרק שמונה שרצים (דך קז:) שהוא פרה ורבה, וכינה הרוחשת אינה פרה ורבה, אלא באה מזיעת אדם. לכך נראה לר"ת, דשחורה הקופצת היא פרעוש וחייב עליה לכ"ע, וכינה הרוחשת שרי להרוג כב"ה המתירין. ובקונטרס נמי פירש בסמוך, דרבה מקטע להו בשבת:
Tosafot on Shabbat 12a:5:1.english: "Lest he kill" - Rabbi Joseph of Orléans explained that a louse [kinah] is the black jumping [insect], for it is written: "And strike the dust of the earth, and it shall become lice" (Exodus 8:12), and it is the nature of the black jumping [creature] to emerge from the earth; and regarding this [species], the Rabbis disagreed with him [Rabbi Eliezer]. However, a flea [par'osh] is the crawling louse, and one is liable for [killing] it even according to the Rabbis, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Shemonah Sheratzim (below, 107b and there). And this does not appear [correct] to Rabbeinu Tam, for we say in the Midrash: "'How much less man, that is a maggot' — these are the lice of the head." And in Niddah, chapter 2 (20b): "He sent her a comb to kill lice [kalmei]," and [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres: "A comb to kill lice"; and it is not the nature of the black jumping [creature] to be on the head. And furthermore, in Berakhot (chapter 7, 51b) we say: "From beggars [one gets] words, and from rags [one gets] lice [kalmei]," and it is the nature of white crawling lice to be in rags of old garments. And furthermore, regarding a flea [par'osh], [the Gemara] says below in the chapter [entitled] Shemonah Sheratzim (107b) that it procreates, whereas the crawling louse does not procreate, but rather comes from human sweat. Therefore, it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that the black jumping [creature] is [in fact] a flea [par'osh], and one is liable for [killing] it according to everyone; and the crawling louse is permitted to kill, in accordance with Beit Hillel who permit [doing so]. And in the Kuntres [Rashi] also explained nearby that Rabba would kill them on Shabbat.

Tosafot on Shabbat 12a:6:1.hebrew: מי אלימא ממתניתין - והפושט ס"ד דברייתא דרכה לפרש טפי ממתניתין. ועוד, דבברייתא קתני: "אין פולין ואין קורין" — משמע טפי דקאי "לאור הנר" אתרוייהו, מבמתני' דקתני: "ולא יפלה את כליו":
Tosafot on Shabbat 12a:6:1.english: "Is it stronger than our Mishnah?" - And the one resolving [the dilemma] thought that it is the way of a baraita to explain more than a Mishnah. And furthermore, since in the baraita it teaches: "One may not delouse and one may not read," it implies more strongly that "by the light of the lamp" applies to both of them, than in the Mishnah, which teaches: "and one may not delouse his clothes."

Tosafot on Shabbat 12a:8:1.hebrew: אפילו להבחין בין בגדו לבגדי אשתו - דרכן היו להיות שוין. מכאן נראה לאסור להבחין בין בגדו לבגדי חברו לאור הנר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 12a:8:1.english: "Even to distinguish between his garment and his wife's garments" - It was their way to be similar. From here it appears that it is forbidden to distinguish between his garment and his fellow's garments by the light of the lamp.

Tosafot on Shabbat 12a:9:1.hebrew: נוטל וזורק ובלבד שלא ימלול - נראה לפרש דאבא שאול כרבנן, וגזר מלילה דכינה אטו מלילה דפרעוש, ומלילה דפרעוש — שמא יהרוג, וכולה חדא גזירה היא. ורש"י פי' דכר' אליעזר סבירא ליה. וקשה, דמשמע דרבי אליעזר סבירא ליה דלפלות נמי אסור, דקאמר לעיל: "לא יפלה — שמא יהרוג, ור' אליעזר היא". ומיהו י"ל דלעיל לא קאי הכי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 12a:9:1.english: "He takes [it] and throws [it], provided that he does not rub [it]" - It seems [correct] to explain that Abba Shaul holds in accordance with the Rabbis, and he decreed [against] rubbing a louse due to rubbing a flea, and [against] rubbing a flea lest he kill [it]; and it is all one decree. And Rashi explained that he holds in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer. And this is difficult, as it implies that Rabbi Eliezer holds that picking [lice from clothes] is also forbidden, as [the Gemara] said above: "He may not pick [his clothes] lest he kill [a louse], and it is [the opinion of] Rabbi Eliezer." However, it can be said that above, [the Gemara] does not stand that way.

Tosafot on Shabbat 12a:9:2.hebrew: רבה מקטע להו - מפרש ריב"א: בחול, וקאי אדרב הונא, דקאמר: "זהו כבודו אפילו בחול". ואנן סמכינן ארש"י, דפי' בשבת, וקיימא כבית הלל דשרו בסמוך:
Tosafot on Shabbat 12a:9:2.english: "Rabba would sever them" - The Riva explains [that this was] on a weekday, and it refers to [the statement of] Rav Huna, who said: "This is his dignity, even on a weekday." And we rely on Rashi, who explained [that this was] on Shabbat; and it stands in accordance with Beit Hillel, who permit [doing so] nearby.
